Automations

The Automations module provides a flexible framework for orchestrating and executing automated processes across connected systems via APIs. It enables the definition, configuration, and execution of workflows that react to events, transform data, and trigger actions in external services without requiring tight coupling or custom integration code.


Automations are intended for:

  • Connect and synchronize data between multiple systems

  • Trigger actions based on events, schedules, or incoming API requests

  • Transform, enrich, and route data between different interfaces

  • Reduce manual processes by encapsulating recurring integration logic

  • Monitor and control automated executions in a centralized way


By abstracting API interactions into reusable automation components, the system allows complex integration scenarios to be implemented in a structured, maintainable, and scalable manner. This makes Automations suitable for both simple task automation and advanced cross-system process orchestration.



Setup OpenCelium

Note

This step is not required when using the cloud version of DataGerry, as OpenCelium is already installed and preconfigured

The Automations module depends on an external integration runtime (OpenCelium) that must be installed and operated locally. A local installation is required in order to execute automation workflows, manage integrations, and handle API communication within your environment.

Before using Automations, ensure that the integration runtime is properly installed and configured. Detailed information about system requirements, installation steps, and initial setup is available in the official installation documentation:

Integration Runtime Installation Guide


Once the local installation is complete configure the credentials in the etc/cmdb.conf file


[Database]
host = 127.0.0.1
port = 27017
database_name = cmdb

[WebServer]
host = 0.0.0.0
port = 4000
ssl = false
certfile = /etc/ssl/certs/cmdb.pem
keyfile = /etc/ssl/private/cmdb.key

[OpenCelium]
host = 127.0.0.1
port = 9090
protocol = http
email = email
user = username
password = password

Set your credentials in the OpenCelium section
